extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, patent prosecutors, IP litigators, patent examiners, and researchers studying patent validity
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing the likelihood a litigated patent will be held valid, using empirical markers from prosecution, claim drafting, prior-art disclosure, and industry patterns derived from Allison & Lemley's 1989–1996 study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidation Rate (baseline)
rubrics_metrics.description: Approximately 46% of fully litigated patents are held invalid in federal court between 1989 and 1996.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ~46% as the empirical baseline against which an individual litigated patent's probability of invalidation should be assessed; note selection effects (see Caveat).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior Art Citation Effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Courts are more likely to invalidate patents based on uncited prior art than on prior art that was disclosed to the PTO during prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This implies examiners' search-and-cite behavior matters substantially for patent durability; weight whether likely invalidating art was cited during prosecution when assessing validity risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity by Ground
rubrics_metrics.description: Among invalidated patents, anticipation (102) and obviousness (103) account for the majority of invalidations; indefiniteness, lack of enablement, and inequitable conduct also contribute; subject-matter eligibility was a smaller share in 1989–1996.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating vulnerability, prioritize analysis of 102/103 exposure but also check for 112 issues (indefiniteness/enablement) and inequitable conduct; adjust for historical shifts in eligibility law (post-Bilski/Mayo/Alice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Robust Prior-Art Search (pre-grant marker)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent whose examiner conducted an independent search and cited diverse prior art (foreign, NPL, multiple classes) is more likely to survive validity challenge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess examiner-cited references breadth (types and classes). A diverse, examiner-developed cited-art record is a positive quality signal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thorough IDS (pre-grant marker)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant disclosure of all material art reduces invalidation risk and avoids inequitable conduct issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether applicants submitted comprehensive IDSs; failure to disclose material art both increases likelihood of uncited invalidating art and raises inequitable conduct risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive Examiner Engagement (pre-grant marker)
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple office actions with substantive 102/103/112 rejections forge a stronger validity record than a single allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Count and evaluate substantive rejections and the prosecution responses—engagement that forces claim construction and record development strengthens post-grant defensibility compared to ‘quick allowance’ histories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cited-Art Dominance (post-grant marker)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is unusual for patents to be invalidated based on art that was cited during prosecution; patents invalidated based on uncited art are more common.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weight whether the universe of art considered during prosecution was comprehensive; patents where probable invalidating references were never before the examiner are at higher risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation Vulnerability (post-grant marker)
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuation patents drafted to capture later-developed competitor products show higher invalidation rates due to written-description and intervening-rights challenges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspect continuations for broad claim scope not supported by the original specification and for possible intervening-rights issues; such structural prosecution choices raise invalidation risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Litigation History / Battle-tested Status
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents that survive multiple validity challenges develop 'battle-tested' status; patents on first litigation are more likely to fall.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider prior litigation outcomes as a positive signal; survival through multiple challenges increases confidence in validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry-Specific Survival Patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: Pharmaceutical patents survive validity challenges at higher rates (~70% upheld); software and business-method patents have lower survival rates; biotechnology patents face high enablement/written-description challenges; mechanical patents are intermediate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust validity expectations by technology sector; consider industry norms and typical grounds of attack (e.g., enablement for biotech, 102/103 for software/business methods).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafting: Submit Comprehensive IDS
rubrics_metrics.description: All art known to applicant or named inventors must be disclosed; broad construction of 'material' art is safer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a drafting/prosecution practice, disclose as much relevant art as possible to reduce uncited-invalidating-art risk and mitigate inequitable-conduct allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafting: Engage Substantively in Prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: Force the examiner to address substantive rejections rather than pursuing quick allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond to and argue substantive rejections to build a record; substantive prosecution creates a more defensible file wrapper than strategies that avoid rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafting: Build Multiple Defensible Claim Layers
rubrics_metrics.description: Include independent and dependent claims at multiple levels of generality to preserve fallback positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft claim sets with layered scope so that narrower fallback claims remain if broader claims are invalidated; this reduces the chance the entire patent is lost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafting: Document Reasonable Inventorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventor-by-inventor contribution records protect against derivation/inventorship challenges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain contemporaneous documentation of contributions and conception/reduction-to-practice to defend inventorship and derivation disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafting: Avoid Functional Claiming Without Structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Functional claiming without structural support invites 112(b) and 112(f) issues, which are common invalidation grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer concrete structural disclosure for claimed functions; ensure the specification provides adequate support for functional language or include structural equivalents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operative Quality Test (assessment checklist)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any issued patent at risk of litigation, ask: How comprehensive was the prior-art universe considered during prosecution? What fraction of likely invalidating art was actually cited? How many substantive office actions did the application receive? Are there continuation-related vulnerabilities (intervening rights, written description, OTDP)? Are independent claims supported by clear specification structure? Is the prosecution history consistent across related applications?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these specific diagnostic questions as a practical scoring checklist; patents scoring high across these items are in the upper tier of the litigated-patent population.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caveat: Selection Effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Litigated patents are not random; they are selected for litigation by parties who believe (rightly or wrongly) the patent is enforceable. Invalidation rates among litigated patents may be lower than among the full universe of issued patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret the 46% invalidation statistic as likely a lower bound on systemic invalidity and adjust evaluations to account for litigation-selection bias.
